facility_desc: Project Bluejay fulfillment center, Hubbell Ave / 500 32nd St SW (developer Ryan Cos.; 780,000 sf proposed in 2019 reports, 645,000 sf in facilities data)
program: City of Bondurant 6-year property tax abatement on new construction (80% yr1 falling 10 pts/yr to 30% yr6; taxes paid on 20% of assessed value in 2022 rising to 70% in 2028 per Register), in development agreement with developer Ryan Cos., approved 4-0 on 2019-11-12; Amazon assumed as owner
issuer: City of Bondurant (council); described in the City FY2024 Financial Information and Operating Report (MSRB EMMA)
notes: Primary: City FY24 disclosure says the Amazon fulfillment center (1/1/2024 actual valuation $261.2M before abatement) has a six-year declining abatement, 80% for FY2022-23 falling to 30% for FY2027-28. Amount: 2.6M is the city administrator's estimate quoted by Des Moines Register 2019-11-12 (secondary; raw/subsidies/IA/desmoinesregister_bondurant_2019-11-12.html, https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/2019/11/12/bondurant-votes-tax-incentives-expected-amazon-warehouse/2575192001/): 'just over $2.6 million during the six-year period' at the minimum $75M assessed value; city to receive about 2.1M in tax revenue. Investment 100M is the developer's committed minimum (Register: cost about 250M per state documents). It is the city's standard package, offered to any developer (Register); Amazon not named in the agreement. KCCI (2019-11, raw/subsidies/IA/kcci_bondurant_approves_bluejay.html) confirms approval of the standard six-year abatement for Ryan Cos. Earlier row (Business Record reprint 2019-11-04, secondary, no amount) folded in. A WHO13 search snippet says the state gave no tax break (page blocked by the site, not opened, not relied on). The actual abatement forgone is not published. Bond/TIF infrastructure in the next row.

facility_desc: Project Bluejay fulfillment center (DSM5) road access: 32nd St SW, Grant St S, U.S. 65 and I-80 ramps (Fortner-Eshelman certified site)
program: Iowa DOT Revitalize Iowa's Sound Economy (RISE) Local Development grant (Iowa Certified Sites), up to 60% of eligible road cost; grant to the City of Bondurant for public roads, not a payment to Amazon
issuer: Iowa Transportation Commission (Iowa DOT); committed 2019-10-08, finalized 2020-01-14
notes: Primary: Iowa DOT FY2020 RISE applications table lists Bondurant: total roadway cost 14,275,472, RISE grant 8,565,283, 40% local match, 'supports creation of over 1,000 new jobs', non-RISE capital investment 250,000,000; commitment of up to 60% approved 2019-10-08 (minutes raw/subsidies/IA/iowadot_commission_minutes_2019-10-08.pdf, Order PPM-2020-21). The DOT table names the company as TBD; the link to Amazon/Project Bluejay is from press: Register 2019-11-12 (city 15.9M infrastructure project, DOT grant 'up to 9.5M', balance by TIF-backed bond) and Business Record (https://www.businessrecord.com/texas-entity-pays-60-8-million-for-site-of-amazon-fulfillment-center/; improvements over 12M). Amounts differ by stage (9.5M early estimate vs 8.57M final); use 8.57M. Overlaps with the city 15.9M infrastructure project (same money). Public infrastructure, not a payment to Amazon. A separate June 2019 RISE award to Bondurant (about 7.7M, Vermeer expansion) is unrelated to Amazon and excluded.

facility_desc: Project Omega: 270,000 sf sorting station adjacent to the fulfillment center (probably DSM9, Shiloh Rose Pkwy SW)
program: City of Bondurant development agreement with Amazon to provide or reimburse the developer for public infrastructure, funded by Series 2021A GO annual-appropriation bonds repaid from tax increment (TIF); Amazon guarantees a minimum assessment of 20M from assessment year 2022
issuer: City of Bondurant (City FY2024 Financial Information and Operating Report, MSRB EMMA)
notes: Primary: the City's own bond disclosure describes the Project Omega development agreement 'with Amazon' and the Series 2021A bonds issued to fund the infrastructure; TIF revenue of about 1.05M a year (FY2024-25 and FY2025-26 on 42.4M assessed value) is the expected repayment source. 6,050,000 is the original principal of the Series 2021A 'City Improvements' bonds shown in the same report; the report does not state the cost of the Omega infrastructure separately, so treat the amount as an upper bound, not a stated agreement amount. Public infrastructure, not a payment to Amazon. Match of Project Omega to DSM9 is by description (a 270,000 sf sort station next to the FC that opened in 2021); not confirmed by address. Agreement document and council minutes not obtained.

facility_desc: MLI1 robotics fulfillment center, Eastern Iowa Industrial Center, 2022 Research Parkway (developer Seefried Industrial Properties; 2.9M sf in the agreement, 2.3M sf per the City; the earlier '~640,000 sf' was wrong)
program: Iowa DOT RISE Local Development (Certified Site) grant to the City of Davenport for road improvements (Hillandale Rd, Research Pkwy, Northwest Blvd, 76th St, N Division St, I-80 ramp lane), up to 60% of eligible cost; 40% city match. City development agreement with Seefried obliges the City to build these improvements; no tax abatement or payment to Amazon found
issuer: Iowa Transportation Commission (Iowa DOT), 2021-12-14 (commitment 2021-05-11); City of Davenport council approved the Seefried development agreement 2021-05-12
notes: Primary: Commission Order TD-2022-43 awards a RISE grant of 2,940,887 or up to 60% of eligible cost, whichever is less, total estimated project cost 4,901,478, city match 40%, from the city share of RISE funds. Commitment first made 2021-05-11 (raw/subsidies/IA/iowadot_media_1440_commission_minutes_2021-05-11.pdf; FY2021 table iowadot_rise_applications_FY2021.pdf lists non-RISE investment 250,000,000 and 1,000 jobs). City side: development agreement with Seefried Industrial Properties (raw/subsidies/IA/davenport_seefried_development_agreement_2021.pdf; resolution 2021-05-12; https://davenport.novusagenda.com/AgendaPublic/AttachmentViewer.ashx?AttachmentID=22304&ItemID=15453): developer builds the Research Parkway extension at its own expense, City builds the other improvements 'without regard to its source of funding' by 2022-08-01, developer spends at least 100M, 1,000 permanent jobs; the cost-estimate exhibit is not in the posted PDF. Earlier row (KWQC 2021-07-07, secondary, 3.9M infrastructure cost, grant 60% and TIF-abated bonds for the rest) replaced: the DOT total is 4.90M, not 3.9M. CORRECTION of the earlier note: the '6.4M city package (forgivable loans, tax rebates)' belongs to Fair Oaks Foods (bacon plant), not Amazon (KWQC 2023-07-13, raw/subsidies/IA/kwqc_davenport_amazon_fairoaks_2023-07-13.html), so no such row. Public infrastructure, not a payment to Amazon. The agreement does not name Amazon (end user unnamed, 'contingent on end-user agreements'); Amazon link from press and the City 2025 release.

facility_desc: 270,000 sf middle-mile distribution facility on 50 acres, 3860 S 24th St (Amazon.com Services LLC owner); sort center SNE1 and the HMW4 listing share this address
program: City partial property tax exemption (abatement) for 10 years under Iowa Code 404.3, South Pointe Urban Revitalization Area, Resolution 22-53
issuer: City Council of Council Bluffs, adopted 2022-02-14
notes: Primary: Resolution 22-53 approves the tax abatement requested by Amazon.com Services LLC for the 2022 assessment year; eligible costs of 30,000,000 were incurred in calendar 2021; applicant requested a 'partial tax exemption for a ten-year period' (the exemption schedule is not stated in the resolution). No dollar value of the abatement is stated, so amount_usd is blank. investment_promised holds the eligible costs incurred, not a promised figure. Address matches facilities.csv F0583 and F0584 (HMW4 and SNE1) exactly. Resolution 23-65 (raw/subsidies/IA/councilbluffs_resolution_23-65.pdf) is for an unrelated owner and is not a row. No IEDA or TIF award found for this site.

facility_desc: 53,230 sf last-mile delivery facility, 6417 Innovation Drive, West Viking Road industrial park expansion lots 12-13 (developer Ryan Companies, then Amazon.com Services LLC)
program: City of Cedar Falls Agreement for Private Development (land conveyance, subsidy_type given as abatement) with Ryan Companies US: 9 acres of free city-owned land plus a five-year declining tax abatement (75%, 60%, 45%, 30%, 15% of the increase in value); minimum assessed value 4.75M; Amazon assumed all obligations
issuer: Cedar Falls City Council (item 3, 2023-08-07; unanimous vote reported by the Courier)
notes: Primary: the mayor's annotated council agenda for 2023-08-07, item 3: a resolution approving an Agreement for Private Development and deed of city land to Ryan Companies US, 'free city land and five years of tax abatements (our usual offering)', minimum assessed valuation 4.75M. Amount blank: the land value and abatement value are not stated. Secondary detail: Waterloo-Cedar Falls Courier 2023-12-15 (raw/subsidies/IA/wcfcourier_cedarfalls_amazon_land_transfer_2023-12.html, https://wcfcourier.com/news/local/business/real-estate/article_3cd37c50-99df-11ee-a22a-1322729be3ab.html): Ryan acquired the land from the city at no cost, a 50-plus page development agreement, abatement 75/60/45/30/15%, building taxes projected at least 124,248 a year, valuation at least 4M (4.75M with land); Amazon took over the land on 2023-10-18 and assumed all obligations with the City Administrator's consent outside a public meeting. The Courier text was obfuscated for non-subscribers and decoded locally; the agenda page is the stronger source. Agenda packet and the agreement itself not obtained. investment_promised holds the minimum assessed valuation, not a stated investment.

facility_desc: 120,000 sf delivery facility, 7200 Chavenelle Rd (existing warehouse sold to Cardinal Industrial and leased to Amazon; QIW2 and WWI2 listings)
program: none: Amazon did not seek local incentives from the City of Dubuque
